newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal deals sluggish, output uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal deals sluggish, output uncertain.

text.p: Indian soymeal exports were dull this week, with buyers unwilling to enter into fresh contracts due to high prices, traders said on Tuesday.
They said soymeal exporters were hesitant to make new commitments in the absence of estimates of the new soybean crop.
Traders last week said contracts for nearly 300,000 tonnes of soymeal exports had been signed for November, December and January shipments.
"After a very sharp rise in prices, now prices are steady and trading activity is dull," said a trader.

Traders said no new export deals had been signed since Friday. While buyers were offering a maximum of $280 per tonne for January shipments, sellers did not want to lower their prices below $283 and preferred to wait.
The markets in Indore, the hub of India's soybean processing industry, were closed on Monday and Tuesday for a Hindu religious festival.
The last overseas contract of 20,000 tonnes at $302 per tonne for ready shipment was signed on Friday. Details of the contract were not known.
"There is uncertainity about the new soybean crop," said Prakash Vohra, a leading oilmeal trader.
The Indian industry had set a production target of 4.5 million tonnes for 1996/97 (November-October).
But erratic weather conditions delayed sowing in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, which accounts for 80 percent of the country's soybean output.
Traders had said this could delay the harvest and yields might be nearly 20 percent below target.
Plentiful monsoon rains in central Indian during the weekend, followed by good sunshine, were beneficial to the crop, they said.
Currently, Indian soymeal export prices were quoted at $303 f.a.s. per tonne for September-October shipments. But not many buyers were emerging above $300 per tonne, traders said.
Soybeans in the domestic market were currently quoted at 13,000-13,150 rupees per tonne. In plant delivery conditions, soybean was traded at around 10,750-10,900 per tonne.
